sources.title: CDN Cache, Invalidation and Performance: Technical Implementation
sources.snippet: CDN Cache, Invalidation and Performance: Technical Implementation CDN cache stores copies of content on edge servers close to users, reducing latency and load on the origin server. Cache invalidation is the mechanism to update or remove that content before its natural expiration. The combination of effective caching and precise invalidation determines how fast and consistent your content is ...

sources.snippet: Building a CDN Cache Invalidation Strategy That Scales in 2026: Surrogate Keys, Cache-Tags, and Global Purging In modern high-traffic web architectures—spanning breaking news media, global e-commerce catalogs, and dynamic SaaS platforms—the Content Delivery Network (CDN) is the first line of defense.

sources.title: CDN Cache Invalidation Strategies and Patterns
sources.snippet: CDN caching reduces latency and origin load, but cached content can become stale. Invalidation tells the CDN to fetch a fresh copy from the origin. This approach handles four invalidation strategies — URL purge, surrogate key (tag-based) invalidation, versioned URLs, and soft purge — with code examples for Cloudflare and Fastly.

sources.title: Caching for Dollars, Not Hits: An Exact Offline Reference for Cloud-Egress Caching and the Crossover That Decides When It Pays
sources.snippet: When a cache miss fetches from cloud object storage, the bill is per GET request and per byte of egress, not latency. Classic caching minimizes the miss rate, the wrong objective: a rarely but expensively fetched object can cost thousands of times more dollars than a frequently but cheaply fetched one.
